title: How the AI works
intro: Rumbo's AI comes from a company called Anthropic (the AI is named Claude). On the free setup, the Coach, plans and flashcards use Groq instead, and search uses our hand-checked sample list. Here's what the AI does, how we check it, and what it can't do.
find1: You type what you're looking for, in your own words.
find2: Our server sends your request — plus your grade, age, interests and town (never your name) — to the AI.
find3: The AI searches the public web, like you would on Google, and reads the most promising pages.
find4: It writes a short card for each real opportunity it found, with a link to where it found it.
find5: Our code checks every link. If a link wasn't actually in the search results, the card is deleted. That's how we stop the AI from making things up.
find6: A second safety check looks for scam warning signs and hides things that aren't right for your age.
limit1: It only searches public websites. It can't log into Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Discord or any account, and it can't see private groups or posts.
limit2: It can miss things. Many local opportunities are only on flyers or announced at school — ask your counselor too.
limit3: Information online can be old or wrong. Always check dates, costs and rules on the official page or by calling.
limit4: When it isn't sure, it says “Not listed, check with organizer” instead of guessing.
limit5: The Coach can make mistakes, too. It's a study helper, not a doctor, lawyer, or counselor.
suggest: Sometimes there's no posted listing for what you want. Then the AI suggests kinds of places that might offer it (like law firms or the courthouse for law internships) and gives you a polite email and phone script. These are clearly labeled — call or email first to ask.
cost: AI searches cost money, so Rumbo saves results for 24 hours (repeat searches are free), gives each device a daily limit, and has a daily budget for the whole app. If the limit is reached, you'll see sample results until tomorrow.
demo: If the app isn't connected to the AI, it shows real programs from a sample list we checked by hand, and the Coach gives simple example answers. These are labeled “Sample.”
safety: Before anything goes to the AI, the app checks for signs that you might be in danger. If so, it shows trusted help lines right away. The AI is also told to refuse anything that isn't right for students and to point you to a trusted adult for serious problems.
